title: Evaluate the Game Tree (Tree DFS)
real_world_story: Before the engine plays a move it needs one number that describes the position: the score that each side can force when both players always pick their best continuation. That number is computed by evaluating the game tree from the bottom up.

real_world_connection.input_represents: The tree of possible continuations where each leaf carries the score of a finished position
real_world_connection.query_represents: The value of the root position
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Scoring every child first and combining the scores with max on the engine's turns and min on the opponent's turns

problem_statement: The engine stores a game tree as a parenthesised expression. An integer is a leaf whose value is the score of a finished position, and ( a b c ) is an internal node whose children are the sub-trees written between the brackets. Node types alternate with depth: the root at depth 0 is a MAX node, its children at depth 1 are MIN nodes, their children are MAX nodes again, and so on. A MAX node takes the largest value of its children and a MIN node the smallest, while a leaf keeps its own score. Evaluate the tree and report the value of the root.
task: Return the minimax value of the root position.
input_format: A single line containing the game tree expression, with single spaces between its parts.
output_format: Print the value of the root position.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes in the tree <= 2000
The expression contains only integers, parentheses and single spaces

examples.explanation: The root is a MAX node. Its children are the leaf 3 and the MIN node (-1 5), whose value is -1, so the maximum of 3 and -1 is 3.

expected_algorithm.name: Tree DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: A depth-first post-order traversal scores every child before its parent, so each node can combine its children's values with max or min exactly once.

complexity.time: O(N) where N is the number of nodes, because every node is evaluated once
complexity.space: O(D) recursion depth where D is the depth of the tree

hint: Parse the expression into a tree before evaluating it.
A leaf simply returns its own score.
An internal node evaluates all of its children first and then keeps the largest value on a MAX level and the smallest on a MIN level.
real_world_takeaway: Depth-first evaluation of a game tree with min and max levels is the minimax rule that every board game engine is built on.
